title: Define metering sanity-check KPIs (drift, freshness, null/duplicate rates) + reporting cadence
creator: Chris Osei
project: Billing meter hardening + pricing experiment integrity (Finance/Legal/RevOps + Product + Eng)
description:
Why this exists
- We’re currently using a mix of ad-hoc queries + spot checks to validate billing meters. This is too brittle given (a) ongoing meter fixes (retries/idempotency, region dimension, embeddings batching), and (b) pricing experiments that depend on high-integrity usage telemetry.
- This ticket defines the shared KPI/SLO targets for metering sanity checks so Finance/RevRec, Product, and Engineering are aligned on: what “good” looks like, what pages vs creates a task, and how we review exceptions.

Scope
- Hosted API usage events → billing ledger → customer-facing usage exports (primary)
- Dedicated GPU-seconds v2 sanity signals (secondary: aligned with same framework)
- KPI definitions, thresholds, alert severity, review cadence, and ownership. (Implementation lives in ENG tickets.)

Non-goals
- Implementing the dashboard/alerts themselves (see ENG-4415 / ENG-4421 / ENG-4438).
- Deciding pricing/packaging changes (separate pricing experiment workstream).

Definitions (shared language)
- “Usage events”: row-level telemetry emitted per billed request/segment used for aggregation.
- “Billing ledger”: invoice-grade aggregated table used by RevRec/Accounting as the basis for invoicing and rev rec.
- “Usage export/API”: customer-facing aggregation (daily + by model/region/account) returned via Usage API / exports.
- “Drift”: absolute difference between (usage events aggregated) vs (billing ledger aggregated) for the same window + dimensions.
- “Freshness”: lag between event occurrence_time and availability in downstream tables/exports.

Proposed KPI / SLO set (v1)

1) Correctness: Ledger vs Usage Events Drift
- Metric: drift_pct = |sum(usage_events.billed_amount_usd) - sum(ledger.billed_amount_usd)| / max(sum(ledger.billed_amount_usd), $1)
- Primary windows:
  - Daily (UTC day)
  - MTD (month-to-date)
- Primary dimensions:
  - org_id/account_id, product (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank), model, region, pricing_plan (if available)
- Thresholds (initial; can tune after 2 weeks of baseline):
  - P0/PAGE: drift_pct >= 0.50% for any enterprise account OR absolute_drift_usd >= $1,000/day (any account) OR drift affects >= 5 accounts in same region/model slice
  - P1/TICKET (no page): drift_pct between 0.20% and 0.50% for any account with >= $500/day usage
  - P2/LOG: drift_pct between 0.10% and 0.20% (monitor)
- Notes:
  - Drift checks should exclude known-approved “shadow billing compare” windows unless explicitly flagged (PM-1872). We still log drift, but alert severity is reduced if change_control_id is present.
  - For experiment analysis, we must segment pre/post meter-fix cutovers and avoid mixing in a single time series.

2) Freshness: Usage Event and Ledger Availability
- Metric A: p99 lag from request_end_ts → usage_events availability
  - Target: p99 <= 30 minutes
  - P0/PAGE: p99 > 90 minutes for 2 consecutive checks
- Metric B: p99 lag from request_end_ts → ledger availability
  - Target: p99 <= 4 hours (ledger is allowed to be slower; invoice-grade)
  - P0/PAGE: p99 > 12 hours OR any continuous “no new ledger rows” gap > 2 hours during business day
- Metric C: daily usage export completeness by 06:00 UTC
  - Target: 99.9% of days available by 06:00 UTC; if not, post incident note + expected ETA
- Month-end close “freeze window” considerations:
  - During freeze, late-arriving events are tracked in a separate “late_events_after_freeze” bucket and require Finance approval before inclusion (see Finance thread: 1770061189-month-end-close-usage-freeze-window).

3) Data Integrity: Null/Invalid Dimension Rates
- Required fields (Hosted API): org_id, account_id, request_id, endpoint, model, region, event_ts, idempotency_key (or server_generated_dedupe_key), prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, billed_tokens, billed_amount_usd, currency
- Metric: null_rate(field) per day and per endpoint/model/region slice
- Thresholds:
  - P0/PAGE: null_rate(org_id/account_id/model/region/event_ts/billed_amount_usd) >= 0.01% OR any nulls for ledger keys (invoice_line_id, invoice_period)
  - P1/TICKET: null_rate(other required fields) >= 0.05%
- Special case: “region” is high sensitivity due to margin/pricing attribution. Any spike in missing region > 0.005% pages SRE + Telemetry (see ENG thread 1770069017 + PR-27541).

4) Data Integrity: Duplicate / Idempotency Violations
- Metric A: duplicate_rate(event_id) over a 7-day rolling window
  - Definition: distinct event_id / total events
  - Thresholds:
    - P0/PAGE: duplicate_rate >= 0.05% (platform-wide) OR >= 0.10% in any single region
    - P1/TICKET: duplicate_rate between 0.01% and 0.05%
- Metric B: idempotency_key collision rate (same idempotency_key + org_id producing >1 billable usage row)
  - P0/PAGE: any sustained collisions (>= 50 collisions/hour) OR any collisions for top-20 revenue accounts
  - P1/TICKET: sporadic collisions with clear backfill/replay cause (documented)
- Metric C: “double count suspicion” heuristic
  - Example: ratio of billed_tokens to raw_tokens or billed_tokens spikes correlated with retry/fallback events (ties to ENG-4430, PR-27463)
  - P1/TICKET: anomaly score above threshold; manual review required

5) Consistency: Usage API vs Ledger (Customer-Facing)
- Metric: drift between Usage API/export and ledger by org/day/model/region
- Thresholds:
  - P0/PAGE: any mismatch that affects invoice preview for enterprise accounts OR any mismatch >= $500/day for any account
  - P1/TICKET: mismatch >= $100/day sustained for 3 days
- This is the metric Support will use first for disputes (ties to SUP-28451).

Cadence + Owners
- Daily automated check (job + dashboard): owned by Eng SRE / Observability (Aisha Bello) + Telemetry (Logan Wright).
- Daily Slack digest (business days): post to #finance and #eng-sre with:
  - top drift slices, freshness p99, null/dup rates, open incidents, and “change_control_id” notes if in shadow billing
- Weekly 30-min review (Finance + Product + Eng):
  - Owner: Talia Benson
  - Attendees: Emily Stone (RevRec), Rishi Malhotra (FP&A), Nikhil Sharma (PM), Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (Telemetry), Aisha Bello (SRE)
  - Agenda: new alerts, resolved items, threshold tuning, upcoming meter changes (PM-1872)
- Month-end: integrate into close checklist and require sign-off artifact (Emily Stone + Laura Bennett).

Acceptance criteria
- A single “Meter Sanity KPI v1” section exists in the metering sanity dashboard spec and is referenced from the on-call runbook.
- Engineering dashboard/alerts implement at least: drift, freshness, null_rate, duplicate_rate, and usage_api_vs_ledger checks with these thresholds (or explicitly documented deltas).
- Finance/RevRec signs off that thresholds are usable for month-end close and invoice preview.
- Product Ops signs off that experiment readouts will segment pre/post meter changes using the defined cutover markers.

Open questions
- Should drift be evaluated in tokens, USD, or both? Proposal: alert primarily on USD drift; include tokens drift as diagnostics.
- Do we need a separate threshold for free-tier accounts (very low denominators cause noisy % drift)? Proposal: apply minimum $ threshold as above.
- How to handle backfills: auto-suppress alerts when backfill_flag = true vs require manual annotation?
